metadata.title: Claude, In Order
metadata.subtitle: The Productivity Plugin

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. You installed Cowork and you want to know which plugin to turn on first. The answer is the one that runs under everything else — and this is how it works.
beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive install question and corrects it to the real one: the plugin that runs under everything else.

show.event: writer types 'Which Cowork plugin should I install first? It’s the one for managing tasks.'
backspaces 'managing tasks' and types 'running your day' on the spoken correction

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A plugin is a Cowork package that extends what Claude can do in a conversation. The foundation layer is the always-on base plugin that holds your context across sessions, sitting under your specialists. And global settings are persistent context — your role, your method — that Claude applies every session.

terms.meaning: a Cowork package that extends what Claude can do in a conversation
the always-on base plugin that holds your context across sessions
persistent context — your role, your method — Claude applies every session

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisite definitions, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Start with the box. This is the productivity plugin — the generalist of the Cowork collection. Where other plugins pick a domain, this one picks a subject. That subject is you.

shot.visual_intent: A sealed cardboard box with terracotta tape drops onto the cream stage and settles. The label 'plugin' appears beside it. Then 'the generalist' rises beneath, in dim ink.
shot.motion_claim: The hero box arrives and its label declares it the generalist — not a domain specialist.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one hero object on cream stage, minimal labels; negative space is the style; underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Every other plugin in this collection points outward — deep into one domain. Sales. Legal. Finance. The productivity plugin points inward — at the day you're working through. Same engine, opposite aim.

shot.visual_intent: Three small domain boxes sit on stage; ink arrows draw outward from each, labeled Sales, Legal, Finance. The center box — the plugin — gets a terracotta arrow that reverses and points inward, toward a label 'you'.
shot.motion_claim: Outward domain arrows fan away; the plugin arrow reverses inward toward 'you'.

show.event: outward arrows draw to Sales, Legal, Finance labels
center box highlighted; terracotta arrow reverses inward

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: directional diagram with four objects on cream stage; underfill waived.

beats.narration_text: Inside it are five moves. Track tasks. Prep for meetings. Triage your inbox. Stay aware of your schedule. And synthesize your notes. Not five apps — five things Claude can now do inside the conversation you're already having.

shot.visual_intent: The hero box lid lifts; five labeled pages rise out in narration order — Tasks, Meetings, Email, Schedule, Notes — and fan into a row in front of the box.
shot.motion_claim: Five pages emerge from the box, one per spoken move, naming each capability as it appears.

show.event: Notes page rises; five pages settle in a fan row

beats.narration_text: You install it and it's live — immediately. No accounts to link, no connectors to authorize. That's rare in this collection and it's why most people put it in first.

shot.visual_intent: The hero box sits on stage beside a toggle switch. The toggle flips on; the box glows with a warm light; a terracotta check mark appears above it. No cable connects to any server.
shot.motion_claim: Toggle flips; the box lights up instantly with no connection cables — live on install.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: hero box + toggle on cream stage; underfill waived.

beats.narration_text: One optional add-on: your calendar. Without it the plugin is still useful — it just can't see your time. Connect one and Claude crosses a line: now it knows what's committed, what's free, and where focus blocks can go.

shot.visual_intent: A usefulness bar sits at mid-scale beside the hero box. A calendar tile appears to the left; a single cable draws from the tile to the box. The bar jumps past a threshold line marked 'time-aware'.
shot.motion_claim: A connecting calendar cable tips the usefulness bar past a visible threshold.

show.event: calendar tile appears; cable draws to box

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: bar + calendar tile + box on cream stage; underfill waived.

beats.narration_text: Tell Claude how you already prioritize and it adapts. Say you use an urgency-versus-importance matrix — that's how it lays your options out: four quadrants, your rule, not its default.

shot.visual_intent: A flat row of task pages from B02 sits on stage. On the spoken word 'matrix', the pages fly into four quadrant zones; axis labels 'Urgent' and 'Important' appear on the grid edges in ink.
shot.motion_claim: Task pages self-sort into a four-quadrant grid on the spoken method, enacting the adopted rule.

show.event: flat task page row on stage
pages fly into four quadrant zones

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: quadrant grid on cream stage; underfill waived.

beats.narration_text: And it compounds. The more Claude knows about your recurring commitments and working patterns, the more useful it becomes. You don't front-load any of it — context accrues naturally, one conversation at a time.

shot.visual_intent: A usefulness curve starts flat then climbs as small terracotta dot marks accumulate along a session timeline below it; each mark lands on the spoken phrase 'one conversation at a time'.
shot.motion_claim: Session marks accumulate along the timeline; the curve climbs with each addition.

beats.narration_text: Think in layers. Your domain plugins — sales, legal, whatever you run — sit on top. The productivity plugin sits underneath all of them, holding the day together while they do specialist work.

shot.visual_intent: A wide base plate labeled 'Productivity' settles on the stage first. Two narrower domain plates descend and stack above it in narration order, each labeled 'a domain plugin'.
shot.motion_claim: Base plate anchors first; domain plates stack above it, showing the foundation relationship.

show.event: base plate drops and settles, labeled 'Productivity'
first domain plate lands on top

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: layer stack on cream stage; underfill waived.

beats.narration_text: You swap specialists in and out as your work changes. The base holds — session after session, carrying your tasks and context forward. It's the one you never turn off.

shot.visual_intent: On the layer stack from B07, a top domain plate slides off and a new one drops in; the base plate stays lit throughout. A terracotta pulse on the base marks each swap. The base plate never dims.
shot.motion_claim: Top plates cycle out and in; base plate stays lit — the always-on foundation.

show.event: second domain plate swaps; base plate remains steady

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I just installed the productivity plugin. Ask me what I spend most of my time on and where my time leaks. Then ask how I already prioritize — deadlines, a matrix, whatever I use. Draft a morning-briefing routine around my real schedule, and tell me the one thing to put in global settings so you remember it every session. That last question is the trick: it turns a one-off chat into a standing setup. Run it, and watch which questions Claude asks before it answers. Then check two things yourself: does every item on the plan trace to something you actually told it? And what breaks when urgent work arrives that Claude never saw?
